txt_167: The myths that keep people from starting treatment
txt_168:
Every chapter of the textbook has a section ‘Myths and False Beliefs’ —
        104 chapters, around a thousand breakdowns. Here are four of them: the ones that most often
        stand between a person and help.
txt_170:
“Depression is simply sadness,
          it can be removed by an effort of will”
txt_171:
Depression is a condition with mechanisms, a course
          and a treatment. Willpower does not work not because the person is weak,
          but because that is how the illness is built. Antidepressants do not cause
          dependence and do not change personality — this is one of the seven myths in the chapter.
txt_172:
Clinical Psychiatry · chapter on depressive
          disorders · 11 myths with breakdowns
txt_173: The full list of myths about depression
txt_175:
“Anxiety is an ordinary feeling,
          not a medical condition”
txt_176:
An anxiety disorder is a diagnosis with criteria,
          not a character trait. And it is not treated by “trying not to be anxious”: a person
          cannot learn not to be anxious by an act of will, any more than they can
          order themselves not to be ill.
txt_177:
Clinical Psychiatry · chapter on anxiety
          disorders · 10 myths with breakdowns
txt_178: The full list of myths about anxiety
txt_180:
“OCD is simply a character trait
          linked to cleanliness”
txt_181:
OCD is a disorder in which a person loses
          control over their own actions, and giving yourself permission to perform
          compulsions does not soothe but reinforces the symptom. “Willpower” here
          is not a tool but part of the trap.
txt_182:
Clinical Psychiatry · chapter on OCD ·
          7 myths with breakdowns
txt_183: The full list of myths about OCD
txt_185:
“Punishment or reproach
          will make the child stop”
txt_186:
Enuresis is not stubbornness or laziness, and punishment
          does not treat it but adds shame, which stops parents
          from seeking help in time. This is one of the six mistakes examined in the chapter.
